mainEntity.name: Does an LLC need meeting minutes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most states do not legally require LLCs to keep minutes, but your operating agreement may, and minutes help document major decisions and support liability protection. Banks, lenders and buyers often ask for minutes or resolutions before approving a loan or a sale. Keeping them saves time later.

mainEntity.name: How often should an LLC hold meetings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hold at least one annual meeting and record it, plus record major decisions as they happen. Follow any schedule in your operating agreement. Single-member LLCs can sign one annual written consent for the year's major decisions, with separate ones for big one-off actions.

mainEntity.name: What is a single-member LLC meeting minutes template?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually it is a written consent signed by the sole member, listing resolutions for the year or for a specific decision. That document records the decision the same way minutes would. Banks often ask to see it before opening an account or approving credit.

Usually the person who chaired the meeting and the person who recorded the minutes sign. Single-member LLC? The sole member signs a written consent. Use a printed name, signature and date for each signer, and keep the signed copy with the operating agreement and other company records.

mainEntity.name: What decisions should be recorded in LLC minutes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Admitting members, changing ownership, taking significant debt, buying or selling major assets, opening bank accounts, amending the operating agreement and electing managers. Record each one as a resolution with exact wording and the vote. Why the precision? Banks, buyers and courts will rely on that wording later.

mainEntity.name: Can LLC minutes be kept digitally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in most cases. Signed PDFs stored securely with your other company records work well. Check any record-keeping rules in your state and operating agreement. Keep minutes for the life of the company.
